mechanism_fidelity.rationale: Omissions are the removable configuration parts; restoring elements reduces that configuration. Repeated tests retain failure-preserving reductions, and single-restoration checks establish test-relative 1-minimality. The mapping preserves the source limits concerning interactions, unresolved outcomes, environmental dependence, reduction order and the distinction between reproducibility and unique causation.

target_fidelity.rationale: The inference makes an explicitly bounded contribution to necessity: a singleton failing omission supports necessity with the reference remainder fixed, while larger sets identify jointly consequential removals without claiming individual necessity. The specified interaction comparisons address why alternative support and context dependence can defeat independent feature ranking.

operational_coherence.rationale: Restoring selected omitted elements produces variants whose activation outcomes directly test whether smaller omission sets retain failure. Baseline verification, controlled participant exposure, explicit outcome criteria and unresolved-outcome handling support the stated inference. The procedure withholds minimization conclusions when its prerequisites fail and distinguishes verified endpoints from provisional reductions.

validity.rationale: The mapping preserves delta debugging's reduction mechanism and inferential limits while providing a coherent, bounded way to investigate activation necessity and interactions. Its prerequisite checks are part of the procedure, and no unsupported empirical result is asserted.

uncertainty: No target measurements are supplied, so no particular element's necessity or interaction is established.

Whether valid variants and reproducible reference and omission outcomes can be obtained remains empirically unknown; the mapping explicitly requires checking these prerequisites before drawing conclusions.
